verdict.rationale: ByteAsk documents its own sandbox policy modes. The headless default is read-only and can still build and run under AddressSanitizer, and `--sandbox workspace-write` permits building, testing and writing files. Changes are presented as a diff, with approval required, before anything becomes permanent. However, the evidence never explains what the sandbox actually isolates (filesystem scope, network, external services or data), so separation from production data is only implied. The diff and approval flow is a review gate, not sandbox isolation. Missing for 10: documentation of the sandbox's isolation boundaries (network, filesystem, external data access), an explicit separate test or staging environment for production data, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: If you want the agent to build, test, or write files, pass `--sandbox workspace-write`.
A read-only run can still build your program under AddressSanitizer and run it.
presents a diff for your review before making permanent changes
